rv.q: That said, there are some substantial moral and ethical questions raised in this intriguing and engaging production.
There is some genuinely good work here both in the script and from the players.
Flaishon writes fraught family conflict better than she writes technological satire, and one longs for more scenes set in Rivka's living room.
There is food for thought in this finely performed, but somewhat haphazard tale.
"Memoriam" is intriguing and thought provoking; the satire not always hitting home, but a chilling insight into what could feasibly be just around the corner.
